# lark

> Structured concurrency, resources, streams, actors and application wiring for
> Kotlin on the JDK's virtual threads, with no coroutines and no second effect
> system. Arrow's `Raise` and `Either` are the error model throughout.

Facts worth having before anything else:

- Kotlin 2.4, JDK 25 or newer. Apache 2.0. On Maven Central as
  `io.github.matthewjones372:lark` and sibling modules, all on one version.
- Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`; between them, `X.Y.(Z+1)-SNAPSHOT` is published
  to `https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/`.
- Experimental: everything is tested, and the API can still change.
- Blocking is fine: every fork is a virtual thread. Do not reach for
  `suspend`, a dispatcher or a `CompletableFuture` where a lark call exists.
- A service is a `Module` (a dependency graph) run by `LarkApp` and `runApp`.
  Resources are nodes the graph releases in reverse dependency order; a node's
  `close()` is the graph's job, not the class that holds it.
- Background work is a `Stream` started on the graph's `StreamBackend`
  (usually `Forks()`), not a scheduler or a thread of its own.
- Lark's compiler plugin, applied with `id("io.github.matthewjones372.lark.wiring")`,
  checks every graph as it compiles and warns where code hand-rolls what lark
  ships: `LARK_RUN_NEVER_RETURNS_ON_SHUTDOWN`, `LARK_SCHEDULER_BY_HAND`,
  `LARK_SECRET_AS_STRING`, `LARK_SLEEP_IN_TEST`.

## Modules

- `lark`: `flock`, `parZip`, `parMap`, `raceN`, `resourceScope`, `Schedule`,
  `timeout`, `policy` (retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiter),
  `LarkLocal`, `Clock`, and the log and metrics calls.
- `lark-pekko`: a Pekko dispatcher as the executor, and Pekko's stages awaited
  from a fork.
- `lark-stream`: `Stream<E, A>` as a description, with its failure in the type
  and no backend named.
- `lark-stream-forks`: runs a `Stream` as a pull loop on one virtual thread;
  the usual backend.
- `lark-stream-pekko`: runs a `Stream` on Pekko Streams, with the operators
  that take Pekko's types.
- `lark-stream-actors`: runs a `Stream` on `lark-actor`, an actor per run.
- `lark-stream-test`: `TestStreams` and `TestClock`, every stage on the calling
  thread and time the test moves.
- `lark-test`: `story` (Given, When, Then), `eventually(within)`,
  `capturingLogs`, `capturingMetrics`.
- `lark-app`: an application as a value: `single`, `singleOf`, `closingOf`,
  `boundTo`, `overriding`, `subgraph`, probes, health, `testApp`, `LarkApp`,
  `awaitShutdown`.
- `lark-app-typesafe`: a HOCON section as a node (`config`), every fault at
  once, `secret`, `choosing`, `overridingConfig`, and where each setting came
  from (`origins`).
- `lark-app-liquibase`: a changelog as a node (`migrations`); readers take a
  `Migrated`.
- `lark-app-pekko`: a Pekko typed actor as a node, keyed by its `ActorRef<T>`.
- `lark-app-actor`: a `lark-actor` flock as a node, and an actor as a node.
- `lark-app-cluster`: a `lark-cluster` membership as a node, joined as a HOCON
  section says.
- `lark-app-gradle`: the Gradle plugin `io.github.matthewjones372.lark.wiring`,
  which checks and draws every graph as it compiles.
- `lark-app-compiler`: the K2 checker behind it, which shows the same faults
  and warnings in the editor.
- `lark-otel`: an OpenTelemetry `Context` that crosses a fork; on the classpath
  and nothing else.
- `lark-slf4j`: lark's log lines through SLF4J, annotations in the MDC; on the
  classpath and nothing else.
- `lark-micrometer`: lark's counters, gauges and timers on Micrometer's
  registry; on the classpath and nothing else.
- `lark-kafka`: Kafka as a `Stream` on any backend: commit after the work,
  dead letters, transactions.
- `lark-kafka-pekko`: `lark-kafka` through Pekko's Kafka connector.
- `lark-actor`: an actor as a value and a step on virtual threads, with no
  actor system.
- `lark-actor-journal-jdbc`: `lark-actor`'s journal and snapshots on JDBC.
- `lark-actor-projection`: a journal as a `Stream`, for a read model that
  resumes where it left off.
- `lark-actor-remote`: `lark-actor` across nodes over one TCP connection per
  pair.
- `lark-actor-remote-protobuf`: remote messages in Protobuf.
- `lark-actor-remote-avro`: remote messages in Avro.
- `lark-actor-remote-kotlinx`: remote messages from `@Serializable` classes.
- `lark-cluster`: gossip membership, discovery and downing with no
  coordinator.
- `lark-cluster-kubernetes`: cluster seeds from the pods API, and a Lease.
- `lark-cluster-aws`: cluster seeds from Cloud Map or ECS, and a DynamoDB
  lease.

## What to reach for

| Want | Use |
|---|---|
| a value built once and shared | `singleOf(::Thing)` |
| a value that must be closed, and is `AutoCloseable` | `closingOf(::Thing)` |
| a value given back some other way | `singleOf(::Thing, Thing::stop)` |
| `main` | `object App : LarkApp<Root>()` and `runApp(App)`; `run` parks on `awaitShutdown()` |
| configuration | `config<Settings>("section") { … }` from `lark-app-typesafe` |
| a password or token | `secret("password")`, never `string(…)` |
| a setting that picks a module | `conf.choosing("section", read) { … }` |
| migrations | `migrations("db/changelog.sql")`, then take a `Migrated` |
| readiness | `.probe(name, timeout, attempts, interval) { … }` |
| background work on an interval | `Stream.tick(every)` started on the graph's `StreamBackend` |
| a call to something unreliable | `policy("…") { deadline(…); retry(…); attemptTimeout(…) }` |
| to stop calling something that is down | `guard(CircuitBreaker(…))` in a policy |
| a retry or backoff | `Schedule.exponential(…)`, `Schedule.spaced(…)` |
| a stream that restarts after a defect | `restartOnDefect(schedule)` |
| a log line, a counter, a timer | `logInfo`, `counter(…).increment()`, `timed(…) { … }` |
| a fake in a test | `.overriding(single<T> { … })` |
| a smaller test | `.subgraph<Root>()` and `testApp(module) { root -> … }` |
| a test that waits for something | `eventually(within) { … }`, never `Thread.sleep` |
| a test of something on a timer | `TestStreams` and `TestClock` from `lark-stream-test` |

- [Applications](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/app.md): the graph, starting and stopping, probes.
- [Cookbook](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/cookbook.md): one recipe per task, every one compiled by a test.
